guide.headline: Texas Tech's offense is built to break Colorado today
guide.hook: Texas Tech owns both the ground game and the money downs against a Colorado defense that struggles on both, and Randon Fontenette is the one Colorado player making them pay for it.

items.title: Third-and-long is not a stop
items.what: Texas Tech ranks No. 14 of 138 on passing downs at 40 percent success, while Colorado ranks No. 109 at 32 percent, a 70 percentile point gap. On third-and-7 or more, Texas Tech throws it 80 percent of the time and converts 36 percent, and Colorado allows 37 percent there, ranking No. 125 of 136. That turns a defensive stand into a fresh set of downs.

items.title: Red Raiders stay on schedule on the ground
items.what: Texas Tech's rush success rate is 52 percent, No. 12 of 138 nationally, against a Colorado run defense ranked No. 74 at 41 percent. That is a 45 percentile point edge, enough to keep Texas Tech out of third-and-long altogether. If Texas Tech is past 20 rushing attempts by halftime, the clock and the chains are both working for them.
items.when: First drive and every first down after that.

items.title: Fontenette is already wrecking this game
items.what: Randon Fontenette sits in the top 3 percent of FBS cornerbacks in production, and he is proving it live with 5 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 sack, and 1 PD already in this game. Watch his press technique at the line and his hip fluidity in transition.
items.when: Whenever Texas Tech targets his side on third down.

guide.cardLine: Texas Tech's offense owns both the run and third-and-long against Colorado, but Randon Fontenette already has a sack and a PD trying to stop it.
